issues.body: For an exact head/base match, `grant_pr_disposition` validates `state` and validates a non-null `merged_at` timestamp independently, but never checks that they form a valid GitHub PR state. A record with `state: "open"` and a valid non-null `merged_at` is returned as `merged`. That contradicts the stated field-consistency/fail-closed contract and lets malformed listing evidence suppress an abandoned-enrollment row. The new malformed-field test set covers invalid values but omits this cross-field inconsistency.
issues.fix_hint: Require a non-null `merged_at` to be consistent with `state == "closed"` (and refuse any inconsistent matching record with `GroomError`). Add a test for an exact-matching PR with `state: "open"` and a valid timestamp in `merged_at`, asserting refusal rather than `merged`.
issues.title: Inconsistent open-and-merged PR records are trusted instead of refused

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 2 fixes the prior workflow-seam finding with exact argv tokenization and a job-level disabling-condition assertion, and it adds broad malformed-field coverage for matching grant PRs. The classifier still accepts one internally inconsistent matching record: an open PR with a non-null valid `merged_at`. Because `merged_at` is allowed to dominate without checking its consistency with `state`, malformed API evidence can suppress a genuinely abandoned enrollment instead of refusing the report. This is narrower than round 1, so progress is improving, but the fail-closed contract is not yet complete.
